rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes altering oxide film quality via surface pre-treatments or slight alloy composition adjustments, while the target study deposited an AlCoCrFeNi HEA coating via APS and annealed it. These are fundamentally different kinds of interventions (surface treatment/composition tweak vs. coating deposition).
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis mentions controlled laboratory simulation of chemical-process/nuclear-power conditions (temperature, pressure, pH, chloride), while the target used specific APS parameters, annealing at 550°C, 3.5 wt% H2SO4 electrochemical testing, and 900°C hot-corrosion with Na2SO4/NaCl/V2O5 salt mixtures. The hypothesis lacks the paper's specific processing and testing conditions.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis focuses on a Cr-Mo oxide passive film acting as a barrier and self-healing interface. The target mechanism involves grain refinement, BCC phase, high-entropy/sluggish-diffusion effects, and formation of Al- and Cr-rich passive oxides (including Cr2O3, Fe(OH)3, etc.) to restrict pit/crack development and impede sulphide attack. These are different mechanistic classes (simple Cr-Mo oxide film vs. complex HEA coating effects).
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts lower corrosion rates (weight loss, pit formation, EIS) for specimens with robust passive films. The target predicts and reports higher microhardness, higher polarization resistance, lower corrosion current, and lower hot-corrosion weight gain for the coated/annealed specimen.
